def-td-rectangular-local-equilibrium-fie.physical_scope: Smooth local-equilibrium continuum data on a fixed three-dimensional Euclidean rectangle; this definition adopts no balance law or constitutive law.

def-td-rectangular-local-equilibrium-fie:
## Definition

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval measured in seconds, let $L_1,L_2,L_3>0$ be lengths in metres, and set $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(0,L_i)\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ with closure $\overline\Omega$. A rectangular local-equilibrium field record consists of an open temperature interval $\mathcal T\subset(0,\infty)$, a temperature field $T:\overline\Omega\times I\to\mathcal T$ whose time derivative through order one and spatial derivatives through order two extend continuously to $\overline\Omega\times I$, a function $u\in C^1(\mathcal T,\mathbb R)$ of internal-energy density in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and its volumetric heat capacity $c(T):=u'(T)>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\,K^{-1}}$. The coordinates $x_i$ are lengths in metres, and $T$ is measured in kelvins, using [[def-td-si-quantities]].

The record may also include a heat-flux field $j_Q:\overline\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ with components in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$ and a conductivity field $K:\overline\Omega\times\mathcal T\to\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ with entries in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. The flux and tensor are field data here; no relation between them is imposed by this Definition. In Euclidean coordinates, $\nabla T=(\partial_{x_1}T,\partial_{x_2}T,\partial_{x_3}T)$ and $\operatorname{div}j_Q=\sum_i\partial_{x_i}(j_Q)_i$. On a flat face, $n$ denotes its outward unit normal.

This is a specified regular field class on a fixed rigid body. It does not assert that every physical medium has local-equilibrium fields, nor does it adopt a heat equation, a boundary condition, Fourier's law, or an entropy-production law.

def-td-regular-elastic-collision-model.physical_scope: A three-dimensional single-species classical kinetic collision model with elastic binary events; no hard-sphere limit or microscopic derivation is included.

def-td-regular-elastic-collision-model:
## Definition

Fix a particle mass $m_p>0$ in kilograms and velocity space $V=\mathbb R^3$ with components in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The elastic collision set is
$$Q_{\rm el}=\{(v,w,v',w')\in V^4:v+w=v'+w',\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\}.$$
Thus each allowed event conserves momentum $m_p(v+w)$ and kinetic energy $m_p(|v|^2+|w|^2)/2$. Equip $Q_{\rm el}$ with the Borel sets generated by its relative topology.

Collision-rate data consist of a nonnegative, countably additive, $\sigma$-finite Borel measure $\nu$ on these Borel sets. It is invariant under exchanging $v$ with $w$, exchanging $v'$ with $w'$, and exchanging the incoming pair $(v,w)$ with the outgoing pair $(v',w')$: for each of these maps $S$ and Borel set $E$, $\nu(S^{-1}E)=\nu(E)$. This is the three-dimensional physical restriction of the collision set and exchange conventions in [[def-tdmath-elastic-collision-kernel]], with $\sigma$-finiteness stated explicitly for the product integrals used by the entropy theorem. Its physical units and rate normalization are chosen so the associated weak collision operator has units of density per second. The measure is a declared model input; no differential cross section or microscopic limit is inferred from this Definition.

post-td-fourier-conductivity.physical_scope: A declared local-equilibrium continuum regime with weak enough gradients for a first-order Fourier constitutive approximation; the conductivity may be anisotropic and state dependent, and no numerical coefficient is asserted.

post-td-fourier-conductivity:
## Postulate

For the field record of [[def-td-rectangular-local-equilibrium-fields]], adopt
$$j_Q(x,t)=-K(x,T(x,t))\nabla T(x,t).$$
Here $K$ has entries in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$ and $j_Q$ in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, so the equation is dimensionally consistent. Write $K_s=(K+K^{\mathsf T})/2$ for the symmetric part and assume $z^{\mathsf T}K_s(x,T)z\ge0$ for every $z\in\mathbb R^3$. The antisymmetric part may contribute to the flux but not to the quadratic entropy production.

This is an adopted constitutive model in the stated continuum regime. It is neither a consequence of equilibrium entropy alone nor a universal law for all media. In particular, it does not assert a finite propagation speed or an empirical value for $K$.

post-td-local-energy-balance.physical_scope: A rigid, fixed-composition, nonrelativistic continuum body on the rectangular domain of def-td-rectangular-local-equilibrium-fields, with no volumetric energy source, no matter flux, and insulated outer faces.

post-td-local-energy-balance:
## Postulate

For a field record on $\Omega\times I$ from [[def-td-rectangular-local-equilibrium-fields]], adopt the local balance
$$\partial_t u(T(x,t))+\operatorname{div}j_Q(x,t)=0$$
and the insulated-boundary condition $j_Q(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ on every face of $\partial\Omega$. Both terms in the local equation have units $\mathrm{W\,m^{-3}}$. The boundary condition says that no heat energy crosses the body's outer faces in this model.

This local continuum balance is an additional adopted postulate, with the sign and energy convention of [[post-td-first-law-energy]]. It is not deduced from that global process-record balance. Matter transfer, volume work, internal sources, moving boundaries, and external-field energy require separately specified balance models and are outside this item.

post-td-local-equilibrium-entropy-densit.physical_scope: Fixed-composition local-equilibrium patches of the rigid continuum model; this caloric relation is not asserted for arbitrary nonequilibrium states or every thermodynamic material.

post-td-local-equilibrium-entropy-densit:
## Postulate

For the local-equilibrium medium of [[def-td-rectangular-local-equilibrium-fields]], adopt a local entropy density $s(T)$ measured in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\,K^{-1}}$ with
$$\frac{ds}{dT}(T)=\frac{c(T)}{T},$$
where $c(T)=u'(T)>0$ is the volumetric heat capacity and $T>0$ is measured in kelvins. Equivalently, for a fixed reference $T_{\rm ref}>0$ and reference density $s_{\rm ref}$, set
$$s(T)=s_{\rm ref}+\int_{T_{\rm ref}}^T\frac{c(\theta)}{\theta}\,d\theta.$$
The volume integral of this field is the entropy assigned by this continuum model. This adopts a local thermodynamic relation extending the macroscopic entropy framework of [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]; it does not prove that every evolving medium has such a local entropy density or identify it with an arbitrary finite-system entropy function.

For constant $c(T)=c_0>0$, the adopted relation gives $s(T)=s_{\rm ref}+c_0\log(T/T_{\rm ref})$. This is a restricted constitutive specialization, not a universal equation of state.

post-td-boltzmann-molecular-chaos-model.physical_scope: A single-species classical dilute-gas kinetic model on a periodic rectangular three-torus, with elastic binary collision data and an incoming-pair molecular-chaos closure; it is not an exact many-particle theorem.

post-td-boltzmann-molecular-chaos-model:
## Postulate

Let $\Omega_{\rm per}=\prod_{i=1}^3(0,L_i)$ with opposite faces identified, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval in seconds, and let $f(x,v,t)\ge0$ be a one-particle number density for $x\in\Omega_{\rm per}$, $v\in\mathbb R^3$, and $t\in I$. With $x$ in metres and $v$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $f$ has units $\mathrm{s^3\,m^{-6}}$ relative to $d^3x\,d^3v$; its moments used below are assumed finite. Periodic boundary conditions are imposed in $x$.

Adopt the incoming molecular-chaos closure: at a collision location and time, the incoming two-particle velocity density used in the collision term is $f(x,v,t)f(x,w,t)$. This is a one-sided factorization assumption; no factorization of the outgoing pair and no derivation from reversible many-particle mechanics is asserted.

For the elastic data $Q_{\rm el},\nu$ of [[def-td-regular-elastic-collision-model]], adopt a collision operator $Q_\nu(f)$, with units of $f$ per second, satisfying for every measurable test function $\varphi$ for which the integrals converge absolutely,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\varphi(v)Q_\nu(f)(x,v,t)\,d^3v=\frac14\int_{Q_{\rm el}}\big(f(x,v',t)f(x,w',t)-f(x,v,t)f(x,w,t)\big)\big(\varphi(v)+\varphi(w)-\varphi(v')-\varphi(w')\big)\,d\nu.$$
The adopted kinetic equation is
$$\partial_t f+v\cdot\nabla_x f=Q_\nu(f).$$
The equation and weak collision identity are model postulates. This item does not assert a hard-sphere Boltzmann–Grad limit, propagation of chaos, or universal equilibration.
lem-td-rectangular-poincare:
## Statement

Let $d\ge1$, let $L_1,\ldots,L_d>0$, and let $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^d(0,L_i)$. If $w\in C^1(\overline\Omega,\mathbb R)$ has zero mean, then
$$\int_\Omega |w(x)|^2\,dx\le \frac d2\sum_{i=1}^d L_i^2\int_\Omega |\partial_iw(x)|^2\,dx\le C_\Omega\int_\Omega |\nabla w(x)|^2\,dx,$$
where $C_\Omega=\frac d2\max_iL_i^2$. All integrals are the multidimensional Riemann integrals of continuous functions on the indicated closed rectangles, with the usual extension to their interiors.

pthm-td-collision-h-theorem.physical_scope: Conditional kinetic-entropy production for a positive regular solution of the periodic, single-species elastic Boltzmann model with incoming molecular chaos; no many-particle derivation or Maxwellian equality characterization is asserted.

pthm-td-collision-h-theorem:
## Statement

Let $\Omega_{\rm per}=\prod_{i=1}^3(0,L_i)$ with opposite faces identified, and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval. Assume the current conditional mathematical result [[thm-tdmath-regular-collision-entropy]] at its exact draft interface [L1] below. Let $f:\Omega_{\rm per}\times\mathbb R^3\times I\to(0,\infty)$ satisfy the periodic Boltzmann postulate [[post-td-boltzmann-molecular-chaos-model]] and the regularity, integrability, and domination hypotheses in [A2]–[A3]. Fix a positive constant reference density $f_{\rm ref}$ with the same units as $f$, and define the kinetic entropy
$$S_{\rm kin}(t)=-k_B\int_{\Omega_{\rm per}}\int_{\mathbb R^3}f(x,v,t)\log\!\left(\frac{f(x,v,t)}{f_{\rm ref}}\right)\,d^3v\,d^3x.$$
Then
$$\frac{dS_{\rm kin}}{dt}=\frac{k_B}{4}\int_{\Omega_{\rm per}}\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(A-B)\log\!\left(\frac AB\right)\,d\nu\,d^3x\ge0,$$
where $A=f(x,v,t)f(x,w,t)$ and $B=f(x,v',t)f(x,w',t)$; the supplier's $\log A-\log B$ denotes the dimensionless difference $\log(A/B)$ for these positive quantities of equal units. Equality holds exactly when $A=B$ for $\nu$-almost every collision at almost every spatial point. This is a conditional deduction inside the adopted incoming-molecular-chaos kinetic model. The cited mathematical carrier is currently draft and has not received independent proof acceptance; no microscopic derivation, experimental claim, or Maxwellian characterization is included.

pthm-td-fourier-entropy-production.physical_scope: Conditional local entropy and energy balance for a sufficiently regular, fixed-composition local-equilibrium continuum field on a rectangular insulated body with a positive-semidefinite symmetric conductivity tensor.

pthm-td-fourier-entropy-production:
## Statement

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval, $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(0,L_i)$ a fixed rectangle, and $(T,u,j_Q,K)$ a field record from [[def-td-rectangular-local-equilibrium-fields]] satisfying the adopted local-energy, Fourier, and local-entropy postulates [[post-td-local-energy-balance]], [[post-td-fourier-conductivity]], and [[post-td-local-equilibrium-entropy-density]]. Assume additionally that $j_Q$ and its first spatial derivatives are continuous on every compact subset of $\overline\Omega\times I$. Then, throughout $\Omega\times I$,
$$\partial_t s(T)+\operatorname{div}\!\left(\frac{j_Q}{T}\right)=\frac{(\nabla T)^{\mathsf T}K_s(x,T)\nabla T}{T^2}\ge0,$$
where $K_s=(K+K^{\mathsf T})/2$. For every compact time interval $[t_0,t_1]\subset I$, the model's total entropy $S(t)=\int_\Omega s(T(x,t))\,dx$ is differentiable and nondecreasing, while $\int_\Omega u(T(x,t))\,dx$ is constant. These are conditional deductions of the declared continuum model, not observations or a claim that every medium obeys Fourier's law.

pthm-td-constant-conductivity-neumann-ex.physical_scope: Existence and uniqueness for the three-dimensional rigid Fourier heat model with constant positive volumetric heat capacity and scalar conductivity, homogeneous Neumann walls, and even-periodic uniformly regular positive initial data; no general rough-data or arbitrary-domain PDE claim is made.

pthm-td-constant-conductivity-neumann-ex:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(0,L_i)$ with $L_i>0$ metres, let $c>0$ be a constant volumetric heat capacity in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\,K^{-1}}$ with $u'(T)=c$ throughout the range of $g$, let $k>0$ be a constant scalar conductivity in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$ with $K\equiv kI_3$ in [[post-td-fourier-conductivity]], and put $a=k/c$ in $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-1}}$.

For $t>0$ define
$$T(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Gamma(x-y,at)g(y)\,dy,\qquad \Gamma(z,\theta)=(4\pi\theta)^{-3/2}e^{-|z|^2/(4\theta)},$$
and set $T(x,0)=g(x)$ on $\overline\Omega$. This field is the unique $C^1$-in-time, $C^2$-in-space solution on each finite time interval of $c\partial_tT=k\Delta T$ on $\Omega$, with $\partial_nT=0$ on every face and the given initial value. It satisfies $T_{\min}\le T(x,t)\le T_{\max}$ for all $t\ge0$, has $C^2$ spatial derivatives continuous to $t=0$, and its right time derivative there is $a\Delta g$. Under [[post-td-local-energy-balance]] and [[post-td-fourier-conductivity]], it is a global-in-time solution of that restricted physical continuum model.

pthm-td-neumann-heat-relaxation.physical_scope: Conditional L2 relaxation for the compatible positive-temperature solution of the constant-capacity, constant-conductivity model on a three-dimensional insulated rectangle.

pthm-td-neumann-heat-relaxation:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the hypotheses and solution $T$ of [[pthm-td-constant-conductivity-neumann-existence]], let $V=|\Omega|=L_1L_2L_3$, define the spatial mean $\overline T(t)=V^{-1}\int_\Omega T(x,t)\,dx$, and put $E(t)=\int_\Omega|T(x,t)-\overline T(t)|^2\,dx$. With $a=k/c$ and $C_\Omega=\frac32\max_iL_i^2$, the mean is constant and
$$E(t)\le e^{-2at/C_\Omega}E(0)\qquad(t\ge0).$$
Thus this model solution converges exponentially to its initial spatial mean in $L^2(\Omega)$; no pointwise-uniform convergence rate is asserted.

rem-td-solution-existence-scope.physical_scope: Source-backed scope and limitation note for the local rectangular Fourier heat model; it reports no experiment and asserts no universal continuum closure.

ex-td-insulated-polynomial-relaxation.physical_scope: An exact initial-profile example inside the constant-capacity, constant-conductivity insulated rectangular model; it is a conditional calculation, not an observation.

ex-td-insulated-polynomial-relaxation:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice as in [[pthm-td-constant-conductivity-neumann-existence]]. Let $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(0,L_i)$, let $c,k>0$, and let $T_b>\epsilon/30>0$, where $T_b$ and $\epsilon$ are in kelvins. For $r\in[0,1]$ set $h(r)=r^2(1-r)^2-1/30$ and prescribe
$$g(x)=T_b+\epsilon h(x_1/L_1)\qquad(x\in\overline\Omega).$$
Use its even $2L_i$-periodic extension in each coordinate as the initial datum on $\mathbb R^3$. The unique insulated heat solution has constant spatial mean $T_b$ and satisfies
$$\int_\Omega|T(x,t)-T_b|^2\,dx\le \frac{\epsilon^2|\Omega|}{2100}e^{-2(k/c)t/C_\Omega},\qquad C_\Omega=\frac32\max_iL_i^2.$$
This gives an exactly computed initial variance and the conditional relaxation estimate of the model.

ex-td-diffusive-infinite-propagation.physical_scope: A mathematical support property of the constant-coefficient Fourier heat model on an insulated rectangle; it is not an observation or a claim about finite-speed physical signals.

ex-td-diffusive-infinite-propagation:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice as in [[pthm-td-constant-conductivity-neumann-existence]]. Let $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(0,L_i)$, choose $x_c=(L_1/2,L_2/2,L_3/2)$ and $0<r<\frac12\min_iL_i$, and define on $\overline\Omega$
$$\phi(x)=\begin{cases}(1-|x-x_c|^2/r^2)^3,&|x-x_c|<r,\\0,&|x-x_c|\ge r.\end{cases}$$
For $L>0$, define the even periodic fold $\rho_L:\mathbb R\to[0,L]$ by $\rho_L(s)=s-2nL$ for $2nL\le s\le(2n+1)L$ and $\rho_L(s)=(2n+2)L-s$ for $(2n+1)L\le s\le(2n+2)L$, $n\in\mathbb Z$. Put $\phi_{\rm per}(x)=\phi(\rho_{L_1}(x_1),\rho_{L_2}(x_2),\rho_{L_3}(x_3))$ and take $g=T_b+\epsilon\phi_{\rm per}$ with $T_b,\epsilon>0$. In the constant-$c,k$ insulated Fourier model, the heat-kernel solution satisfies
$$T(x,t)-T_b=\epsilon\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Gamma(x-y,(k/c)t)\phi_{\rm per}(y)\,dy>0$$
for every interior $x\in\Omega$ and every $t>0$, although the initial perturbation is supported in the compact ball $\overline B(x_c,r)\subset\Omega$. Thus the adopted diffusion model has no finite propagation speed for this temperature perturbation.
